User story: As a local user, I want the app to open an existing or new workspace so I can start work without setup.
Expected behavior based on code: Create/list/state persist across server restart.
Initial test approach: Automated tests plus isolated API restart smoke
Initial test command or route: cargo test --workspace; GET/POST /api/workspaces; restart; GET state
Test result: Fresh isolated smoke created one workspace, restored it after restart, and returned the same current version.

User story: As a Chinese-language user, I want to send text and visibly receive the Agent reply.
Expected behavior based on code: API returns chat reply; composer is IME safe; user, Agent, and errors render in timeline.
Initial test command or route: cd web && npm test; cd web && npm run build
Test result: GH-114 first reproduced 3 renderer failures, then connected chatEntries to MessageRow/AssistantTurn. User, Agent chat, system/error, escaped text, and grouped tool-log tests pass; sendMessage state is re-rendered and reply text is present.
Notes: 2026-07-16 fresh verification: 100 frontend tests and production build passed. Browser runtime smoke was not available.

User story: As a user, I want an Agent proposal to be based on the current graph and applied as an auditable version.
Expected behavior based on code: Current implementation auto-applies valid proposals; stale/invalid bases must be rejected.
Initial test approach: Code/tests; real Codex acceptance requires external runtime
Test result: Proposal unit/integration tests pass with FakeRuntime. No fresh real Codex proposal was executed in this audit.
Errors: Client graph is trusted before apply; real Codex proposal acceptance is still missing.
Notes: Old tracker described pending apply/dismiss behavior and is obsolete after auto-apply commit.

User story: As a user, I want tool/runtime evidence without losing the normal answer.
Expected behavior based on code: Tool logs group under Agent turns and all event streams remain ordered.
Test result: GH-114 now renders the normal answer exactly once alongside its collapsed tool-log group. The separate global eventSeq defect can still drop later Agent session events.
Errors: Per-run/per-session seq is incorrectly treated as a workspace-global cursor.
Notes: Renderer portion passed on 2026-07-16; event ordering remains open.

Feature / capability: Manual run queue and real progress
User story: As a user, I want Run to execute the selected real provider and show truthful progress/results.
Expected behavior based on code: Current server graph is compiled, capability-compatible provider executes, and real artifacts are persisted.
Initial test approach: Mock tests plus isolated empty-graph/API smoke
Test result: Mock orchestration tests pass; isolated empty graph correctly returned 422. Manual real-provider path bypasses cost gate and provider inputs are not materialized.
Errors: A mock succeeded run does not prove real execution.
Notes: No paid provider call was authorized.

User story: As a user, I want every potentially paid run to show a credible estimate and wait for confirmation.
Expected behavior based on code: Manual, Agent, and sweep runs share one estimate/confirm/actual-cost state machine.
Test result: Manual runs bypass estimation; Atlas/FAL estimated and actual costs are hardcoded zero.
Errors: Unknown/paid cost is represented as free and can auto-start.

User story: As a user, I want interrupt to stop both local state and the remote paid task.
Expected behavior based on code: Provider task id persists and remote cancel/reconciliation determines final status.
Test result: Local status can become interrupted, but Atlas/FAL cancel is unsupported and remote ids are not persisted.
Errors: Remote job may continue and bill after UI says interrupted.

User story: As a user, I want auditable graph versions and safe restore.
Expected behavior based on code: Undo/restore create immutable versions and stored bytes match graph_hash.
Initial test approach: Automated tests plus isolated API export/restart
Test result: Sequential version tests pass, but shared non-atomic layout files can make a successful version point to another request's content; reads do not verify hash.
Errors: Concurrent persistence violates immutable-version contract.

User story: As a user, I want to export the current workflow without runtime secrets.
Expected behavior based on code: Export returns current graph schema and rejects unsafe runtime metadata.
Initial test approach: Automated tests plus isolated route smoke
Test result: Fresh isolated export returned schemaVersion 1 and the persisted empty graph.
Notes: Export correctness still depends on fixing graph file integrity.

User story: As a user, I want to inspect the real generated content and download it safely.
Expected behavior based on code: Preview renders real text/media content and download stays inside artifact root.
Test result: Text/JSON preview shows metadata instead of bytes; write path accepts traversing node ids; remote downloads are unbounded.
Errors: Preview is not the generated text and artifact persistence is unsafe.

User story: As a user, I want visible errors and an Agent-assisted minimal fix.
Expected behavior based on code: Failed run/error messages render, and debug proposal uses trustworthy server graph.
Initial test command or route: cargo test --workspace; cd web && npm test
Test result: RunErrorCard and general system/chat error rendering pass after GH-114, but the message/debug path still trusts the client graph before server-side validation.
Errors: Debug proposal input is not yet a trustworthy server-owned graph.
Notes: Visibility fixed on 2026-07-16; graph trust remains open.

User story: As a user, I want a cost-bounded real sweep with one recommended output.
Expected behavior based on code: All sweep jobs are capability-valid, costed, confirmed, and coordinated with other workspace runs.
Initial test approach: Automated mock tests and call-chain audit
Test result: Mock sweep state tests pass; cost is zero, workspace active-run coordination is bypassed, and real-provider acceptance is absent.
Errors: Mock outputs and zero cost cannot validate a paid sweep.

Feature / capability: Primary workbench layout and status affordances
User story: As a user, I want the workbench to truthfully show connection/provider status and results.
Expected behavior based on code: Layout renders all surfaces and provider status reflects a fresh authenticated probe.
Initial test approach: Static render tests; browser environment discovery; catalog smoke
Initial test command or route: cd web && npm test; GET workspace state
Test result: Chat messages are visible after GH-114 and static tests pass. Atlas is still shown healthy from key presence only; browser visual smoke remains unavailable.
Errors: Configured is mislabeled healthy; artifact text preview remains metadata-only.
Notes: Chat visibility fixed on 2026-07-16; provider/preview defects remain open.

User story: As a user, I want to select only a usable provider and keep that choice after restart.
Expected behavior based on code: Unavailable options are disabled; selected provider persists; full graph compatibility is checked.
Initial test approach: Isolated select/restart smoke plus capability audit
Test result: Atlas selection persisted across restart, but selection does not prove health/capability; unavailable providers can still be persisted.
Errors: No graph-wide capability preflight.

User story: As a user, I want to add, move, resize, connect, configure, and delete nodes.
Expected behavior based on code: Catalog has six nodes and valid edits create versions.
Initial test approach: Automated tests plus isolated catalog smoke
Initial test command or route: cargo test --workspace; GET /api/catalog/nodes; cd web && npm test
Test result: Fresh catalog returned six nodes; graph/edit test suites pass.
Notes: Default artifact-to-output drag compatibility remains limited; tracked separately.

User story: As a user, I want local edits to be explicit before Agent/run actions.
Expected behavior based on code: Dirty edit gate blocks conflicting actions; commit/discard updates state and visible errors.
Initial test approach: Frontend unit tests plus renderer audit
Test result: State transitions, dirty-edit gates, commit/discard, and system/error message rendering all pass after GH-114.

User story: As collaborators, we want concurrent comments without loss and stale-base conflict feedback.
Expected behavior based on code: baseSeq is enforced, seq monotonic, updates atomic and idempotent.
Initial test command or route: 40 concurrent POST comment ops with baseSeq=1
Test result: 33 responses were 200 and 7 were 500; only 4 comments remained, seq=5.
Errors: Lost updates and partial-file read errors.

User story: As collaborators, we want live cursor/selection presence.
Expected behavior based on code: Presence POST broadcasts a workspace-scoped WS event.
Test result: Received canvas.presence over WebSocket with actor, cursor, selection, and viewport; POST returned 200.
Notes: Durable run/Agent event ordering is separately failed.

User story: As a user, I want to attach a local image and use it in a workflow.
Expected behavior based on code: Multipart upload persists validated bytes and returns an artifact/upload id wired to input.image.
Test result: No upload route/store method/FormData path exists; paperclip is disabled.
Errors: uploads table is declaration-only and storage_uri is unvalidated.

User story: As a user, I want one idempotent review action and at most one retry.
Expected behavior based on code: Review transition and retry creation are one transaction with an idempotency key.
Test result: Single-request tests pass; overlapping rejects can create multiple retry runs and duplicate provider charges.
Errors: No unique parent/attempt constraint.

User story: As a user, I want cache hits only when the effective provider request is identical.
Expected behavior based on code: Cache key includes effective model/config/catalog/implementation revision.
Test result: Existing cache tests pass, but changing FAL_IMAGE_MODEL does not change the key and no TTL/config invalidation exists.
Errors: Old-model artifacts can be returned after configuration changes.

User story: As a user, I want Atlas to generate real text, image, and video from connected inputs.
Expected behavior based on code: Authenticated health passes; all capabilities consume declared ports; real outputs, polling and costs persist.
Initial test approach: Static contract audit; paid acceptance not authorized
Initial test command or route: Atlas opt-in smoke with budget cap
Test result: Atlas key is configured, but health is synthetic, inputs are ignored, prompt_writer contract is impossible, and costs are zero.
Errors: No successful real capability contract/E2E evidence.

User story: As a user, I want FAL to generate a real image from a connected prompt.
Expected behavior based on code: FAL is selectable only when configured/healthy and consumes materialized prompt input.
Initial test command or route: FAL opt-in smoke with budget cap
Test result: FAL_KEY is unset in the audited environment. Code also ignores connected inputs and reports zero cost.
Errors: Provider unavailable and core contract incomplete.

User story: As a user, I want generated text/media visible in the workbench.
Expected behavior based on code: Text preview fetches actual content; media validates MIME/content before display.
Test result: Text/JSON preview only contains generated metadata lines; frontend does not fetch the content endpoint.
Errors: Actual prompt-writer output is not shown.

User story: As a user, I want follow-up messages to understand prior workspace conversation.
Expected behavior based on code: Agent receives bounded trusted history or resumes a durable Codex thread.
Test result: Every request creates a new session and transcript with only the current user message.
Errors: Persisted workspace messages are never passed to Codex.

User story: As a user, I want progress to survive reconnects without missing or reordering events.
Expected behavior based on code: One global event id or per-stream cursors cover all run/session events.
Initial test command or route: cd web && npm test; cargo test --workspace
Test result: Local per-run/session seq values are compared as one global cursor; Agent events are not persisted for catch-up.
Errors: Legitimate low-seq events can be dropped.

User story: As an operator, I want non-loopback deployments to require authentication and authorization.
Expected behavior based on code: Server refuses public bind without auth; paid mutations require identity/authorization.
Test result: All REST routes are unauthenticated; WS ticket is optional and its issuance endpoint is unauthenticated.
Errors: Public bind exposes workspace and paid-run actions.
Notes: Default loopback reduces but does not remove risk.

User story: As a user, I want truthful message count and first-message preview.
Expected behavior based on code: Backend returns real count/preview or UI leaves fields blank.
Test result: Backend omits these fields and frontend defaults messageCount=0, firstMessage=null.
Errors: Existing conversations can appear empty.

User story: As a user, I want configured, healthy, unavailable, and capability-limited states distinguished.
Expected behavior based on code: Status comes from timestamped real probes; connectors/backends are visible.
Test result: Key presence is labeled healthy; persisted provider status is not used; some catalog sections are hidden.
Errors: UI overstates readiness.

User story: As an operator, I want to follow repository instructions and start the complete app.
Expected behavior based on code: Repo includes a documented same-origin release topology and all required environment variables.
Test result: Axum does not serve dist; no proxy/container/start script exists; README has checks but no actual start/deploy flow.
Errors: Repository cannot be deployed as one complete app from its own instructions.

User story: As a user, I want a declared Agent run action to execute through one validated contract.
Expected behavior based on code: RunRequest skill/output is wired into the message route and same cost/capability gates.
Test result: RunRequest types/helpers exist, but the main route bypasses them with direct classification and run handling.
Errors: Declared execution layer is not the actual startup path.

User story: As an operator, I want readiness to prove dependencies and restarts to use the same data root.
Expected behavior based on code: Readiness checks DB/storage/Codex/provider; data root is stable and explicit.
Initial test approach: Isolated health/restart smoke plus config audit
Test result: Explicit data root restart passed, but health always returns ok and default root depends on process cwd.
Errors: Unready service can appear healthy; different cwd can show empty data.
